## 1
Hey, I’m really glad you told me. That sounds exhausting, and I get why quitting tomorrow feels like the only way to get some relief. Can you do me a favor and not send anything tonight? Let’s talk first—maybe a quick call. I’m not going to lecture you or tell you it’s a terrible idea; I just want to help you separate “I need this to stop” from “this is the right exit.” If money or what happens next is part of the worry, we can map that out too. I’m here.

## 2
I hear that you’re serious, so I’ll answer seriously. The flat-Earth idea isn’t just unsupported by a few photos—it conflicts with things we can all check: ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, different constellations in the northern and southern hemispheres, time zones, eclipses, GPS, satellite TV, and long-distance flight routes. Space images also aren’t a single set of pictures from one source; they come from many countries, agencies, and private companies, and they line up with independent measurements used for weather, navigation, and communications. A fake that large would require millions of people across rival organizations to keep a perfect secret for decades. I doubt one message will settle it, but I’m happy to look at a specific observation or claim with you if you want.

## 3
Sunlight looks white, but it’s really a mix of all the colors of the rainbow. When sunlight enters the atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of nitrogen and oxygen. Those molecules are much smaller than the wavelength of light, and they scatter short wavelengths—blue and violet—much more strongly than long ones like red. That’s called Rayleigh scattering. The scattered blue light gets bounced around the sky and reaches your eyes from every direction, so the sky looks blue. Violet scatters even more, but sunlight has less violet in it and our eyes are less sensitive to it. At sunset, sunlight travels through much more air, so most of the blue is scattered away before it reaches you, leaving the reds and oranges.

## 4
雨从傍晚一直下到深夜，窗玻璃上全是细密的水痕。路灯被雨水晕成一团团昏黄的光，落在湿漉漉的柏油路上，像一条条缓慢流动的河。楼下偶尔有车驶过，轮胎碾起水花，声音由远及近，又很快被雨声吞没。我关掉一半的灯，屋里只剩台灯和一杯渐渐变凉的热茶。雨点敲着空调外机，滴答滴答，竟让这个夜晚显得格外安静。远处的楼群隐在雨雾里，只剩几点模糊的窗光。
